dataset.name: Data and scripts associated with the manuscript "Estimating soil moisture and salinity response to simulated coastal flooding using time-lapse electrical resistivity and induced polarization monitoring”
description: This package contains geophysics datasets generated during the simulated ecosystem-flooding experiment – TEMPEST (Terrestrial Ecosystem Manipulation to Probe the Effects of Storm Treatment). These geophysics data consist of Electrical Resistivity Imaging (ERI) and Induced Polarization (IP) datasets collected to estimate the soil moisture and salinity response to the simulated coastal flooding experiment. In addition to using geophysics datasets to estimate soil moisture and salinity response, petrophysical relationship between the measured resistivity and moisture content and salinity using the multisalinity. This package consists of two folders: “MultiSalinity Experiment” folder and “TEMPEST Experiment and petrophysical conversion” folders. The “MultiSalinity Experiment” folder contains the datasets generated from the multisalinity experiment used to develop the petrophysical reslationship. The “TEMPEST Experiment and petrophysical conversion” folder contains ERI, IP, Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) and Electromagnetic Induction (EMI) datasets collected during the TEMPEST experiment. This study shows the ability to used geophysical datasets in estimating moisture content and salinity at scale will be useful in calibrating Earth System Models.

citation: Adebayo, M.B., Bailey, V.L., Ehosioke, S, Emmanuel, E.D., Hopple, A.M., Regier, P.J., Rod, K.A., Megonigal, J.P., Chen, X., Ward, N.D., Doro, K.O. 2024. Estimating soil moisture and salinity response to simulated coastal flooding using time-lapse electrical resistivity and induced polarization monitoring. Geophysics Journal (in prep)
measurementTechnique: These datasets were generated from the Terrestrial Ecosystem Manipulation to Probe the Effects of Storm Treatments (TEMPEST) experiment that was designed to simulate extreme freshwater and estuarine water disturbance at an ecosystem scale. During the experiment, 265 cubic meter (m3) of estuarine water of salinity with average salinity of 8.1 practical salinity unit (psu) was delivered to the estuarine water plot, and 265 m3 of freshwater of 0.06 psu was delivered to the freshwater plot via a drip irrigation setup described in Hopple et al. (2023). ERI datasets were collected on a 100 m long transect that cut across both freshwater and estuarine water using the Lippmann resistivity system. The Lippmann resistivity system measures both resistivity in Ohm-meter (Ωm) and phase change in millirad (mrad), at a frequency of 10 Hz Additional 42 m long transect across the estuarine water plot only was acquired using an eight-channel (R8) Supersting resistivity meter and a multi-electrode switch box. For the multisalinity experiment, six 10 cm long undisturbed core samples were collected at three different locations (2 core samples at each location). Thereafter, a portable Spectral Induced Polarization (SIP) equipment (from Ontash & Ermac, Inc., NJ, USA) was used to measure the ambient real and imaginary conductivities at 50 different frequencies between 10 mHz and 10 kHz. The SIP measurement was carried out on the six samples at different fluid conductivity in a saturation state using seven different brine solutions.
